title: A doctor for the dark
hook: named a Doctor of the Church in 1926; a guide for anyone in the night

segments.voice: Yesterday, Úbeda, 1591. Dying, John asked to hear the Song of Songs, not the prayers for the dying. Your line was arise and come. Today, the last of eighteen days with little Seneca.

A long, dark stretch can take many shapes. A diagnosis. A grief that won't lift. A prayer life gone flat and silent for months. Some people in that place say the same thing: I thought I was doing it wrong. A small friar, jailed by his own brothers, wrote about that stretch in poems and commentaries. More than three centuries after he died, the Church gave him a title it gives to teachers it holds up for everyone. Today: a doctor for the dark.
screen: `A LONG, DARK STRETCH.` → `I THOUGHT I WAS DOING IT WRONG.` → `A DOCTOR FOR THE DARK.`

segments.voice: First, the word. Doctor comes from the Latin docere, to teach. A Doctor of the Church isn't a physician. It's a teacher the whole Church is told it can trust. The title asks for three things: a holy life, deep learning, and a pope's declaration. It's rare. The first four were named in 1298: Ambrose, Augustine, Jerome and Gregory the Great. Second, the long road. John died in 1591, mistrusted by some of his own superiors. He was canonized a saint in 1726, and in 1926 Pope Pius XI named him a Doctor of the Church. He's known as the Mystical Doctor. Third, what he teaches. Look back over these weeks. The dark night: when prayer goes dry, God may not be gone. Dry is not gone. The three signs: the longing stays. Nada: nothing, then everything. Remora. The log that smokes before it catches. Together, it fits in one surprising sentence: the dark can be part of the road, not the end of it. Fourth, why it matters on an ordinary Tuesday. John is careful. In the Dark Night he says some dryness comes from melancholy or bad health, and that isn't the night he means. He never makes pain holy for its own sake. What he gives people in the dark is company, and a map. Someone has been here and wrote down the way through. A psalm says it to God, in the Douay-Rheims: "night shall be light as the day." The Mystical Doctor spent his life on that line.
screen: `DOCERE — TO TEACH.` · `CANONIZED 1726, DOCTOR 1926.` · `THE DARK CAN BE PART OF THE ROAD.` · `COMPANY, AND A MAP.` · then, large: `NIGHT SHALL BE LIGHT AS THE DAY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person in a dark stretch right now, and don't try to fix it; just hold their face for a moment. Ask whether it would help them to know someone has walked this road before, maybe through one line from these weeks: dry is not gone. Only if it feels kind, not like a lecture. If you pray, hold them in the quiet.
Mystical Doctor. John of the Cross's title since 1926, a teacher the whole Church can trust, drawn from the Latin for teach. Today's word.
Your line: the night is a way. A way, not a wall. Tomorrow, a new guide.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of St. John of the Cross on December 14, and spiritual directors often point people in long seasons of dryness to his Dark Night and Ascent of Mount Carmel.
